 Ramsey Solutions Says Your Social Security COLA Isn't a Raise - Here's What to Do With It
 Social Security's 2027 COLA is 3.6%, but rising prices could eat into retirees' gains.
 By
 Chris Lewis, CEPF 
 ,
 Edited by
 Laura Hohenstein 
 Updated
 Oct. 23, 2026
 Fact checked 
 This article was subjected to a comprehensive fact-checking process. Our professional fact-checkers verify article information against primary sources, reputable publishers, and experts in the field.
 Add Us On Google
 Google Preferred Sources lets you customize your search results. By choosing to follow FinanceBuzz, you’re telling Google to prioritize content from a source you trust.
Social Security beneficiaries will receive a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) in 2027. The increase will add an average of $75 a month to retirement benefits, bringing the estimated average monthly benefit for retired workers from $2,095 to $2,170.
 Ramsey Solutions cautions that extra COLA cash isn't a raise. It's a 
buffer against rising prices. A larger check doesn't necessarily mean more purchasing power. The COLA is designed to help benefits keep pace with inflation, and the latest price data show that household expenses remain a concern. For retirees living on a fixed income, the key question is how far that additional money will go after essential costs are paid.
 If you want to be as stress-free as possible while living on Social Security , see below how you can make the 
best use of that increase.
 Editor's note: Social Security and COLA data come from the 
Social Security Administration. Inflation figures come from the BLS. Medicare 
data comes from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services. 
 Get a protection plan on all your appliances
 Did you know if your air conditioner stops working, your homeowner’s insurance won’t cover it? Same with plumbing, electrical issues, appliances, and more. 
 A home warranty from Choice Home Warranty could pick up the slack where insurance falls short. 
 For a limited time, you can get your first month free with a Single Payment home warranty plan.

 Recognize the COLA for what it is
The COLA isn't designed to improve your financial situation. Its purpose is 
simply to prevent it from deteriorating. Even with a 3.6% increase in 2027 , your personal expenses could rise faster than your benefit, especially if housing, food, transportation, or health care take up a large share of your income. As of September 2026, inflation is already outpacing the upcoming COLA adjustment at 3.7%
 Treat the adjustment as one part of your income plan, not a reason to assume your budget has more breathing room. Review your actual expenses before deciding whether the increase can go toward savings, discretionary purchases, or bills that have become harder to manage.
 Shopping for cheaper auto insurance? Enter your zip code here to get started. 
 Do a budget audit before making any changes
Before you adjust your spending, make sure you track what your actual expenses 
were over the past 12 months. Grocery, housing, and healthcare costs tend to 
rise faster for older Americans than national averages suggest. 
If your personal cost increase is outpacing 3.6%, the COLA hasn't left you 
ahead. Instead, it's only reduced how much ground you are losing. You need to 
know your real numbers before you can make any significant changes to your 
budget. 
 Direct the increase toward your financial cushion
If, when you do your budget, your expenses are covered, the most practical use 
of the COLA increase is to direct it toward an emergency fund rather than 
discretionary spending. 
Ramsey recommends keeping three to six months of expenses in accessible savings 
when possible. A small, consistent addition to that savings account builds a 
meaningful buffer over time, especially heading into years when the COLA 
adjustment may be even smaller. 
 If you’re over 50, take advantage of massive discounts and financial resources
 Over 50? Join AARP today — because if you’re not a member you could be missing out on huge perks. When you start your membership today, you can get discounts on things like travel, meal deliveries, eyeglasses, prescriptions that aren’t covered by insurance and more.

 Check what Medicare Part B takes first
If you're enrolled in Medicare, Part B premiums are automatically deducted from 
your Social Security check. In 2027, the standard premium is projected to rise to $209.50 per month, up 
$6.60 from $202.90 in 2026. That single increase wipes out a chunk of your 
COLA increase before it arrives. 
 Understand why the COLA calculation works against retirees 
COLAs are based on the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical 
Workers (CPI-W), which tracks spending for working-age people, not retirees. Seniors typically spend a larger share of their income on health care 
than the CPI-W reflects. Advocacy groups have pushed for a senior-specific 
Inflation Index for years. No change has been enacted, so retirees should expect 
COLAs to routinely underestimate their real cost increases. 
 Know that inflation has already overtaken the 2026 adjustment
 The 2026 COLA was 2.8%, but the latest inflation data show that prices have continued to rise faster than that adjustment. In September 2026, the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) was up 3.7% from a year earlier, while the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) rose 3.9%.
 Energy prices climbed 20.4% over the 12 months ending in September, and gasoline prices rose 34.2%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). Those increases can put additional pressure on retirees who rely on their cars or spend a significant share of their income on utilities and other essentials.
 The comparison helps explain why a COLA may not feel like a meaningful raise . When prices rise faster than benefits, a monthly check may cover less than it did a year earlier. Individual experiences will vary depending on spending habits and where someone lives, but retirees should compare their own expenses with their benefit increase rather than assume the adjustment fully offsets inflation.
 Retirement News: Almost 80% of Americans fear a retirement age increase — here’s the real reason why 
 Consider part-time work or a lower-cost location
For retirees whose budgets are particularly squeezed between the COLA and actual 
prices, finding part-time work to supplement their income could be a good 
solution as long as health and circumstances allow. 
Alternatively, some retirees consider moving to a location with an overall lower 
cost of living. Both of these options reduce dependence on the annual COLA and 
give retirees more direct control over their retirement budget. 
 Build retirement income that doesn't depend on Social Security
More than a third of men and nearly half of women over 65 rely on Social 
Security for at least half of their income. Without Congressional action, Social 
Security trustees project the program may not cover full benefits past Q4 2032. 
Ramsey recommends investing 15% of your household income for retirement, starting with a 401(k) match and then a Roth IRA. The 
idea is that the less you have to depend on the COLA, the less damage it does 
to your retirement plan when it falls short. 
 Bottom line
Social Security's 2027 COLA will increase benefits by 3.6%, adding an estimated $75 a month to the average retirement benefit. But the adjustment doesn't guarantee that retirees will gain purchasing power. September inflation was 3.7% for the CPI-U and 3.9% for the CPI-W, with energy and gasoline prices rising even faster. 
The reminder that the COLA is a maintenance tool at best is important for retirees to keep in mind. Plus, of course, right now, the 
2026 COLA has fallen well below current inflation. The smarter move to protect your retirement 
plan is to reduce how much it depends on Social Security in the first place.
Paying off debt before leaving the workforce, building tax-advantaged savings, 
and finding income sources outside government programs are steps that can change your financial picture in retirement. A stronger personal 
finance foundation means a below-average COLA affects your life far less.
